meta_description: The question is not whether to fine-tune but who owns the resulting model risk.

blocks.x: The question is not whether to fine-tune but who owns the resulting model risk.

Why Fine-tuning is a governance decision, not a modeling one: because the differentiated advantage has moved to the data layer and the operating model around it. The technology is the commodity; the discipline is the moat.

items: Curated corpora beat corpus size; licensing and PII posture decide auditability.
LoRA/QLoRA economics make iteration weekly: if the registry and eval gates exist.
EU AI Act technical documentation is cheapest when generated during training, not after.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: Ask for the baseline: how was the starting position measured, and who signed it?
Ask for the trail: can your auditors replay any decision the system made last week, end to end?
Ask for the unit cost: what does one decision cost to run, and who owns keeping it down?

blocks.x: We can describe exactly where Fine-tuning is a governance decision, not a modeling one programs stall, because we have inherited enough of them: contract-less integrations, drift without owners and dashboards nobody alerts on. The pattern exists to prevent precisely these.

items: Every stage has a gate with real stop authority — scope expands on measured deltas, not on momentum.
The operating model is designed first — who decides what, at which gate, holding which evidence.
Evidence is generated while the work happens, so the audit is a walkthrough, not an archaeology project.

blocks.x: Domain evals typically gain +15-25 points over frontier prompting after disciplined adaptation.
